name: Web design & development
title: Web Design Melbourne for Small Businesses | CodeMax
heading: Web design for Melbourne small businesses
description: Melbourne web design and development for small businesses. Explore responsive websites, redesigns and practical SEO foundations with CodeMax.
intro: Your website should make it easy to understand your business and take the next step. CodeMax brings design and development together for Melbourne businesses that need a new website or a clearer, more useful existing one.
sections: Start with the job your website needs to do

A service business may need phone calls and quote requests; a creative business may need a portfolio that explains its work. Tell us who your customers are, which services matter most and what you want visitors to do. Those decisions guide the page structure, content and contact flow.
Design for the phone in your customer’s hand

Responsive layouts, readable text and clear navigation help visitors use your website across screen sizes. We consider image sizes, form fields and tap targets alongside the visual design. Your content should be available as ordinary page text, with meaningful headings and links.
A redesign starts with your existing content

Share your current website and the pages you want to keep. Existing articles, service URLs and useful images need a migration plan before a replacement goes live. We can discuss page titles, descriptions, internal links and redirects as part of that scope.
What affects the cost of a small business website?

A focused service website and an online shop need different budgets. Page count, copywriting, photography, booking or payment integrations and the condition of an existing website all affect the quote. Separate the initial design and build from domain renewal, hosting, business email, paid software and ongoing support. This makes it easier to compare proposals on the same scope.
A practical brief for your new website

Tell us your main service, the customers you want to reach and the action you want them to take. Include your existing website if you have one, pages you need, examples of designs you like, your budget and any launch deadline. If the budget is limited, prioritise a clear service page, genuine examples of your work and an easy way to request a quote.
Web design in Malvern East, serving Melbourne businesses

CodeMax is based in Malvern East. We work with Melbourne small businesses on new sites and redesigns, combining website structure, visual design and ongoing support. A local service website should explain where you work, what customers can book or request, and how to contact you. Useful local detail matters more than repeating suburb names.
A redesign example: the CodeMax website

Our own redesign brings the existing article collection into the new website alongside focused service pages. Existing articles stay at their original addresses, while the new enquiry form uses a security check before sending email. It is an example of planning around content you already have, rather than discarding it when the design changes.
faq: How much will my website cost?

The scope determines the quote: page count, content preparation, design work, forms, integrations and migration all affect the work involved. Send your goals and budget so we can discuss a practical starting point.
Can you redesign my existing website?
Yes. Share its URL and explain what is not working for your visitors or your business. We can review what to retain, what to improve and how to handle the changeover.
Can you build a website for a tradie or local service business?
Yes. The brief can focus on your services, the areas you actually cover, project photos and quote requests. Tell us if you need click-to-call, booking links or separate pages for different services.
Can I keep my domain and business email?

A redesign can often retain your domain and email setup. We review the current hosting, DNS and email records before planning a change. Tell us who manages each service so the handover can be scoped correctly.
Does a new website include SEO?

Our web design scope can include crawlable pages, descriptive titles, internal links and a sitemap. Content campaigns, local business listings and ongoing reporting are separate work to agree in the quote. A new design alone cannot guarantee a ranking.

name: SEO content & web marketing
title: SEO Content Writing Melbourne | CodeMax
heading: SEO content that explains what you do
description: SEO content writing and web marketing support for Melbourne businesses. Plan useful service pages, articles and internal links with CodeMax.
intro: Getting found begins with pages that answer the questions your customers actually ask. CodeMax offers SEO article writing and web marketing support, with content organised around your services and audience.
sections: Match each page to a customer’s question

A person comparing website providers needs different information from someone learning how local search works. Service pages should explain the offering, scope and next step. Articles can explore a specific question in more detail and link readers to a relevant service.
Make your expertise visible

Useful content needs details from your business: what you deliver, who it suits, how it works and examples you can substantiate. We can help shape those details into readable copy. AI-assisted drafting still needs human review for accuracy, originality and relevance.
Measure useful traffic, not just more words

Search Console data can show which queries lead to impressions and clicks. Combined with enquiry data, it helps identify pages worth improving. Rankings and traffic are not guaranteed; a good content plan gives each page a purpose and checks its results over time.
faq: Will SEO content guarantee first place on Google?
No. Content is one part of search performance, alongside competition, technical accessibility and other signals. We focus on useful, accurate pages rather than ranking promises.
Can existing articles be improved?
Yes. Share the article URLs and, if available, Search Console results. We can discuss which questions need clearer answers and which older details need reviewing.

name: Website maintenance & support
title: Website Maintenance & Support Melbourne | CodeMax
heading: Practical website support in Melbourne
description: Website maintenance and technical support from CodeMax in Melbourne. Discuss content changes, hosting needs and a practical plan for your existing website.
intro: A website needs attention after launch. CodeMax provides custom technical support and helps businesses plan the changes and maintenance their website actually needs.
sections: Start with the issue you are seeing

Send your website address, a description of the problem and the device or browser where it occurs. Screenshots and the steps that trigger an error are useful. We can then discuss whether the issue concerns content, layout, hosting, forms or another integration.
Match maintenance to your website

A static brochure website and a site using a content management system have different requirements. Content edits, software updates and backups should be considered in relation to the technology in use. The support scope, responsibilities and any recurring costs need to be agreed for your setup.
Keep ownership and ongoing costs clear

Hosting, domain registration and business email are separate services, even when one provider manages them. We can discuss your current arrangement and what should be kept. Before moving a website, existing email and DNS records need to be accounted for.
Small updates or a larger repair?

For a content update, send the page address and the exact text or image to change. For a broken form or layout, include a screenshot, device and the steps that reproduce the problem. These details help establish the scope before a quote; passwords should only be shared through an agreed secure method.
faq: Do I need a monthly maintenance plan?
That depends on the platform and how often the site changes. Tell us what is running your website and the help you need; the appropriate scope can then be discussed.
Can you help with a website built by someone else?
Share the URL and platform details first. We need to assess the existing setup and available access before confirming what support is possible.

name: Graphic design
title: Graphic Design for Melbourne Businesses | CodeMax
heading: Graphic design for a consistent business identity
description: Graphic design for Melbourne businesses from CodeMax. Discuss brand visuals, marketing graphics and artwork that works across your website and social channels.
intro: Your website, social content and marketing material should feel like they belong to the same business. CodeMax offers graphic design to help create a clear and recognisable visual identity.
sections: Build from your existing brand

Share your logo, colours, fonts and any brand guidelines you already use. If the visual direction needs work, examples of what you like can help explain the style you are aiming for. We discuss the audience and purpose before choosing a design direction.
Design for the place the artwork will appear

A website banner, social post and printed piece each have different dimensions and viewing conditions. Tell us the required formats and where the design will be used. Print work also needs the printer’s specifications for size, bleed and colour.
Keep your message easy to read

Good visual hierarchy makes the main message clear, with supporting details and a visible next step. We balance typography, imagery and spacing so the artwork serves the communication task. Website and social media work can be discussed together for a more consistent result.
faq: What should I provide for a design brief?
Send the wording, images you have permission to use, brand assets, intended audience, required sizes and deadline. Include any printer or platform specifications.
Can the artwork match my existing website?
Yes. Share your website and current brand assets so we can discuss a design direction that fits the existing identity.

name: Social media kit
title: Social Media Design & Content Melbourne | CodeMax
heading: Social media content with a consistent look
description: Social media kits, graphics and reels for Melbourne businesses. Discuss your audience, content needs and brand direction with CodeMax.
intro: CodeMax helps businesses bring their brand into the conversation through social content and reels. Start with a clear message, a recognisable visual style and content suited to the channels you use.
sections: Give each post a purpose

A post might introduce a service, answer a common question or show a piece of work. Decide what the audience should understand and what action makes sense. A useful brief includes the channel, audience, key message and any offer details that need checking.
Connect social content with your website

Social profiles can bring people to a service page, portfolio or contact form. Keeping the wording and visual style consistent helps visitors recognise your business when they move between channels. Campaign destinations should answer the promise made in the post.
Plan the content you can support

Photos, short clips, product details and genuine examples give content something specific to say. Share the assets you have and the formats you need. We can discuss graphics, reels and AI-assisted creative work, with final content reviewed for accuracy and brand fit.
faq: Do you offer social graphics and reels?
Yes. Tell us the platforms, formats and volume you need so the work can be scoped.
Does a content kit include posting or account management?
Deliverables and account responsibilities need to be agreed in the quote. Let us know if you need content production only or additional help.

name: Website & competitor analysis
title: Website & Competitor Analysis Melbourne | CodeMax
heading: Understand what your website needs next
description: Website and competitor analysis for Melbourne businesses. Review content, navigation and the customer journey with CodeMax before planning your next changes.
intro: A useful website review should help you decide what to improve first. CodeMax offers web and competitor analysis to understand your market and guide practical digital decisions.
sections: Review the visitor’s journey

Start with the pages where customers arrive. Can they understand the service, find relevant examples and make contact easily? Navigation, mobile readability and form behaviour can all affect that journey. A review should connect each finding to a real user task.
Compare relevant competitors

Businesses serving the same audience provide useful reference points. We can look at how they explain services, organise content and answer buying questions. The aim is to identify missing information and opportunities to communicate your own strengths, rather than copy another website.
Prioritise the next changes

Broken links and unclear enquiry paths may need attention before new visual effects. Content gaps, technical issues and wider redesign work should be weighed against the business goal. If you have analytics or Search Console data, it can help distinguish assumptions from observed behaviour.
What to include in your review request

Share your website address, the service you want more enquiries for and the area you serve. Mention whether visitors are not finding the website, leaving without contacting you or encountering a technical problem. Those are different issues, and each needs different evidence and a different next step.
faq: What do you need to review my website?
Send the website URL, the services you want to grow and a few competitors your customers consider. Existing analytics can help, but the initial discussion can start without them.
Does a review mean I need a new website?
Not necessarily. Targeted changes may address the most important problems. The review helps decide whether updates or a larger redesign make sense.
